{{Kyoto School}} [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
IT is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref>
== Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

{{Kyoto School}} [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
IT is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref>
== Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

{{Kyoto School}} [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
IT is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

{{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
IT is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

{{draft}}{{complex}} {{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
IT is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

{{draft}}{{complex}} {{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
IT is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

revision.comment: [[西田幾多郎#思想]] へのリダイレクトを解除しました
revision.text:
[[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.ja.svg|thumb|場所の論理 [//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b5/File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.ja.svg SVGで表示（対応ブラウザのみ）]]] [[西田幾多郎]]によって開発された哲学的枠組みである「場所の論理」は、京都学派の創設者である著名な日本の哲学者によるものです。<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>。これは彼の成熟した哲学体系の基石とされています。<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> 基本的に、場所の論理は現実の階層的なシステムという考えであり、各レベルまたは「場所」はその下のレベルの性質を包含し決定します。西田によると、究極の現実は「絶対無」であり、存在と非存在を超えた無限の可能性と創造性の源です。<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
この理論は、西洋哲学の伝統的な概念からの出発とされています。<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
また、「善の探求」と「自己意識における直観と反省」の書籍で取り上げられています。<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>
これはコラとは異なる概念です。<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref>
== 場所と場所の論理 == 「場所」という言葉は日本語です。「場所」または「トポス」という意味です。[[西田幾多郎]]はこの用語を彼の業績で使用しました。彼は意識が異なる「場所」またはトポイを占めると述べました。<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
西田はトポイの階層を作成しました。それらは抽象的なものから具体的なものへと範囲が広がります。最も抽象的なトポスは普遍です。これらは判断や命題で使用されます。次のトポスは意識です。彼はこれを相対的無のトポスと呼びました。これは意識の対象と比較して「無」です。その次は反射的自己認識のトポスです。ここでは見ること、知ること、欲することが起こります。これより上は「知的世界」のトポスです。ここで、創造的自己は価値を求めます。これらの価値には真実、美、善が含まれます。西田は究極のトポスを絶対的無と見ました。このトポスは記述や断定を超えています。<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
西田が提案したトポイの階層： 1. 直接体験の場所：西田は「純粋体験」から始めます。これは、感じる人と感じられるものの間に分裂がない単純な状態です。ここでは、誰が体験しているか、何が体験されているかについて考えることなく、すべてが直接体験されます。 2. 意識的自己認識の場所：次に、彼は自己認識（自覚、jikaku）について語ります。これは心が自身を見つめる場所です。自分の考えについて考えるときのようなものです。この場所は、心が自身とそれが認識しているものを同時に知ることについてです。 3. 客観的現実の場所：これは私たちが関連する外部の世界です。イマヌエル・カントの現象学的世界に類似しています。 4. 歴史的世界の場所：このレベルは、時を通じて共に生きる人々についてです。人々がどのように行動し、自己を表現し、社会の中で他者とどのように生活するかを含みます。これは人間の生活と歴史の大きな絵についてです。<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> 5. 絶対無の場所：最後に、西田は絶対無（絶対無、zettai mu）という考えを紹介します。これは通常の人間の経験を超えた現実です。無の場所と絶対無の場所。<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref> ==脚注==

この理論は、西洋哲学の伝統的な概念からの出発とされています。<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />

J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>
これはコラとは異なる概念です。<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref>

西田が提案したトポイの階層： # 直接体験の場所：西田は「純粋体験」から始めます。これは、感じる人と感じられるものの間に分裂がない単純な状態です。ここでは、誰が体験しているか、何が体験されているかについて考えることなく、すべてが直接体験されます。 # 意識的自己認識の場所：次に、彼は自己認識（自覚、jikaku）について語ります。これは心が自身を見つめる場所です。自分の考えについて考えるときのようなものです。この場所は、心が自身とそれが認識しているものを同時に知ることについてです。 # 客観的現実の場所：これは私たちが関連する外部の世界です。イマヌエル・カントの現象学的世界に類似しています。 # 歴史的世界の場所：このレベルは、時を通じて共に生きる人々についてです。人々がどのように行動し、自己を表現し、社会の中で他者とどのように生活するかを含みます。これは人間の生活と歴史の大きな絵についてです。<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # 絶対無の場所：最後に、西田は絶対無（絶対無、zettai mu）という考えを紹介します。これは通常の人間の経験を超えた現実です。無の場所と絶対無の場所。<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>

この理論は、西洋哲学の伝統的な概念からの出発とされています。<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
また、「善の探求」と「自己意識における直観と反省」の書籍で取り上げられています。<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. また、「善の探求」と「自己意識における直観と反省」の書籍で取り上げられています。<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>
これはコラとは異なる概念です。<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref>
== 場所と場所の論理 == 「場所」という言葉は日本語です。「場所」または「トポス」という意味です。[[西田幾多郎]]はこの用語を彼の業績で使用しました。彼は意識が異なる「場所」またはトポイを占めると述べました。<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
西田はトポイの階層を作成しました。それらは抽象的なものから具体的なものへと範囲が広がります。最も抽象的なトポスは普遍です。これらは判断や命題で使用されます。次のトポスは意識です。彼はこれを相対的無のトポスと呼びました。これは意識の対象と比較して「無」です。その次は反射的自己認識のトポスです。ここでは見ること、知ること、欲することが起こります。これより上は「知的世界」のトポスです。ここで、創造的自己は価値を求めます。これらの価値には真実、美、善が含まれます。西田は究極のトポスを絶対的無と見ました。このトポスは記述や断定を超えています。<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
西田が提案したトポイの階層： # 直接体験の場所：西田は「純粋体験」から始めます。これは、感じる人と感じられるものの間に分裂がない単純な状態です。ここでは、誰が体験しているか、何が体験されているかについて考えることなく、すべてが直接体験されます。 # 意識的自己認識の場所：次に、彼は自己認識（自覚、jikaku）について語ります。これは心が自身を見つめる場所です。自分の考えについて考えるときのようなものです。この場所は、心が自身とそれが認識しているものを同時に知ることについてです。 # 客観的現実の場所：これは私たちが関連する外部の世界です。イマヌエル・カントの現象学的世界に類似しています。 # 歴史的世界の場所：このレベルは、時を通じて共に生きる人々についてです。人々がどのように行動し、自己を表現し、社会の中で他者とどのように生活するかを含みます。これは人間の生活と歴史の大きな絵についてです。<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # 絶対無の場所：最後に、西田は絶対無（絶対無、zettai mu）という考えを紹介します。これは通常の人間の経験を超えた現実です。無の場所と絶対無の場所。<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>

{{draft}}{{complex}} {{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
It is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />
