{{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Logic of basho]][[en:draft:Logic of basho]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Logic of basho|Logic of basho]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}}{{draft}}{{complex}} {{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
It is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

It was then copied to userspace on simple english wikipedia and edited before being imported here. The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here [[every:Logic of basho|Logic of basho]] and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Logic of basho]][[en:draft:Logic of basho]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}}{{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Logic of basho]][[en:draft:Logic of basho]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Logic of basho|Logic of basho]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}}{{draft}}{{complex}} {{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
It is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}}{{draft}}{{complex}} {{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
It is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}}{{draft}}{{complex}} {{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
It is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}}{{complex}} {{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
It is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

{{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
It is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />

{{Kyoto School}}[[fr:Logique de Basho]] [[File:Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi.svg|thumb|Nishida's hierarchy of Topoi[[fr:logique du lieu]]|440x440px]] {{Nihongo|The Logic of Basho|場所の論理|Basho no ronri}}<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com">{{Cite web|title=Logic in Japan - Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|url=https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/logic-in-japan/v-1/sections/nishidas-logic-of-basho-and-logic-of-the-predicate|access-date=2023-06-08|website=www.rep.routledge.com|language=en}}</ref> is a {{ill|Philosophy|lt=philosophical|en}} framework developed by {{ill|Kitaro Nishida|lt=Kitaro Nishida|en}}, a prominent Japanese philosopher and founder of the {{ill|Kyoto School|lt=Kyoto School|en}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-20 |title=THE LOGIC OF BASHO |url=https://archive.ph/wip/e1Ab1 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=The Kyoto School of Philosophy |language=en}}</ref>. It is considered "the cornerstone of his mature philosophical system".<ref name="The Logic of Nothingness">{{cite book|url=https://www.booktopia.com.au/the-logic-of-nothingness-robert-j-j-wargo/book/9780824829308.html|title=The Logic of Nothingness}}</ref> [[fr:Utilisateur:Immanuelle/logique du lieu]] At its basic level the Logic of Basho is an idea of a hierarchical system of reality where each level or "place" envelops and determines the nature of the levels below it. The ultimate [[reality|reality]], according to Nishida, is "absolute nothingness," a source of infinite potentiality and [[creativity|creativity]] beyond being and non-being.<ref name="Maraldo-2019">{{Citation|last=Maraldo|first=John C.|title=Nishida Kitarō|date=2019|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/nishida-kitaro/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Winter 2019|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2023-06-08}}</ref>
It marked a departure from traditional [[Western philosophy|Western philosophy]] by Kitaro Nishida.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
It was covered in the books ''An Inquiry into the Good and Intuition and Reflection in Self-Consciousness.<ref name="Wargo-2005">{{Cite book|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvn1pf|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitaro|last=Wargo|first=Robert J. J.|date=2005|publisher=University of Hawai'i Press|isbn=978-0-8248-2930-8|jstor=j.ctvvn1pf}}</ref>''
It is a different concept than Chora.<ref name="Schroeder-2019">{{Cite journal|last=Schroeder|first=Brian|date=2019-10-02|title=Hiding Between Basho and Chōra|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/15691640-12341430|journal=Research in Phenomenology|volume=49|issue=3|pages=335–361|doi=10.1163/15691640-12341430|issn=0085-5553}}</ref> [[fr:Logique de Basho]] == Etymology == The term Basho no Ronri is a slightly less formal phrasing. Ronrigaku is the term for formal logic and ronri is a more informal term.<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> Basho is sometimes translated as {{ill|Topos (disambiguation)|lt=topos|en}},<ref name="www.rep.routledge.com" /> or "place".<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
The terms Ba (場) and Basho (場所) do not indicate empty spaces but spaces with things in them<ref name="Hanks-2019">{{Cite journal|last1=Hanks|first1=William F.|last2=Ide|first2=Sachiko|last3=Katagiri|first3=Yasuhiro|last4=Saft|first4=Scott|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoko|last6=Ueno|first6=Kishiko|date=2019-05-01|title=Communicative interaction in terms of ba theory: Towards an innovative approach to language practice|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216618306222|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|series=Quo Vadis, Pragmatics?|language=en|volume=145|pages=63–71|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2019.03.013|issn=0378-2166|s2cid=155749281}}</ref>.<ref name="Unno-2007">{{Cite journal|last=Unno|first=Mark|date=2007|title=The Logic of Nothingness: A Study of Nishida Kitarō (review)|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/44/article/219081|journal=The Journal of Japanese Studies|volume=33|issue=2|pages=554–558|doi=10.1353/jjs.2007.0086|issn=1549-4721|s2cid=144651818}}</ref>
Nishida first coined the term in 1926.<ref name="weebly">https://iajp.weebly.com/uploads/2/6/2/4/26244939/2022april_jjp_vol_nishida_cfp.pdf</ref>
== Self-Awareness and World == Nishida questioned how people think about consciousness. He focused on self-awareness. He believed self-awareness was key to understanding consciousness. He said that without self-awareness, consciousness would be like a mechanical reaction. It would not explain awareness. He claimed that self-awareness has a logical structure. This structure links it to the world of objects..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida saw awareness as self-reflexive. He compared it to an infinite set reflecting in its subsets. He thought the world had self-awareness. This is because it reflects in everything that exists. Nishida believed individual self-awareness is part of this larger reflection. He changed how people think about consciousness. He did not see it as just an individual trait. He saw it as a wide field. This field extends beyond the individual. It mirrors the world..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Topos and the Logic of Place == The term "Basho" is Japanese. It means "{{ill|place|lt=place|en}}" or "{{ill|topos|lt=topos|en}}." Nishida used this term in his work. He said consciousness occupies different 'places' or topoi..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida created a hierarchy of topoi. They range from abstract to concrete. The most abstract topos is universals. These are used in judgments or propositions. The next topos is {{ill|consciousness|lt=consciousness|en}}. He called this the topos of relative nothingness. It is a 'no-thing' compared to the objects of consciousness. After this is the topos of reflexive self-awareness. This is where seeing, knowing, and desiring happen. Above this is the topos of the "intelligible world." Here, the creative self seeks values. These values include {{ill|truth|lt=truth|en}}, {{ill|beauty|lt=beauty|en}}, and {{ill|Good and bad|lt=goodness|en}}. Nishida saw the ultimate topos as absolute {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}}. This topos is beyond description and predication..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
Nishida proposed this hierarchy of topoi # The Place of Direct [[Experience]]: Nishida starts with "pure experience." This is a simple state where there's no split between the person feeling and the thing felt. Here, everything is just experienced directly, without thinking about who is experiencing or what is being experienced. # The Place of [[Consciousness|Conscious]] [[Self-awareness|Self-Awareness]]: Next, he talks about [[self-awareness]] (自覚, jikaku). This is where the mind looks at itself. It's like when you think about your thinking. This place is about the mind knowing itself and what it's aware of at the same time. # The Place of Objective [[Reality]]:This is the outside world we relate to. Analogous to the {{ill|Phenomenology|lt=phenomenological|en}} world of Immanuel Kant. # The Place of the [[History|Historical]] [[World]]: This level is about people living together through time. It includes how people act, how they express themselves, and how they live with others in society. It's about the big picture of human life and history.<ref>https://nirc.nanzan-u.ac.jp/journal/3/article/138/pdf/download</ref> # The Place of Absolute Nothingness: Finally, Nishida introduces the idea of absolute no-thingness (絶対無, zettai mu). This is a reality past normal human experience. Mu no Basho and Zettai Mu no Basho.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw">{{Cite web|title=Identity and the unity of experience: A critique of Nishida's theory of self|url=http://buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw/FULLTEXT/JR-ADM/putney.htm|access-date=2023-06-08|website=buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw}}</ref>
== Me-Ontology == Nishida had a logical view of topoi. He also had an ontological perspective. He called this 'me-ontology.' This term comes from the Greek word 'meon.' 'Meon' means non-being. The topos of being describes the natural world. The topos of relative {{ill|nothingness|lt=nothingness|en}} is consciousness. It contrasts with the topos of being. Absolute nothingness underlies both. It transcends their differences.<ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> Nishida used the Japanese term '{{ill|zettai|en}}.' This means absolute.<ref name="buddhism.lib.ntu.edu.tw" /><ref name="Maraldo-2019" /> It also suggests breaking through or overcoming opposition. He used this term to explain his idea..<ref name="Maraldo-2019" />
== Applications == It has been applied in [[urban planning]].<ref name="studylib.net">{{Cite web|title=The logic of place (basho no ronri) was a fundamental theme in the|url=https://studylib.net/doc/7456207/the-logic-of-place--basho-no-ronri--was-a-fundamental-the...|access-date=2023-06-08|website=studylib.net|language=en}}</ref>
Nishida criticized Greek {{ill|hylomorphism|en}}, {{ill|Immanuel Kant|lt=Kantian|en}} [[Dualism (philosophy of mind)|dualism]], and {{ill|Edmund Husserl|lt=Husserlian|en}} {{ill|phenomenology|en}}<ref name="Kitarō-2012">{{Cite web|last1=Kitarō|first1=Nishida|last2=Krummel|first2=John W. M.|date=2012|title=The Unsolved Issue of Consciousness|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/KITTUI-2|access-date=2023-06-08|website=philarchive.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com-2">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151241055?redirectedFrom=fulltext|access-date=2023-06-08|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref name="academic.oup.com">{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/6968/chapter-abstract/151239473?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false|access-date=2024-03-26|website=academic.oup.com}}</ref> and [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]]'s metaphysics.<ref name="academic.oup.com-2" /><ref name="academic.oup.com" />
